Macrons

Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

most adjective and pronoun

the greater part, the majority

also most of, most people, most of the time, mostly, for the most part, the majority

classical

Quint. 4.2.31: plērīque scrīptōrēs
Cic. Inv. 1.65: multī nihil prōdesse philosophiam, plērīque etiam obesse arbitrantur (Lewis & Short)

plērīque, plēraeque, plēraque

adjective, plural (the singular plērusque is rare and post-classical)

most, most people, the greater number

It agrees with its noun, plērīque Belgae (Caes. BG 2.4), or takes ex (Lewis & Short). Often no stronger than “very many”.

Other words

  • maxima pars — most (of), the greatest part

    noun phrase, with a genitive of the whole · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 1.1: magna pars vītae ēlābitur male agentibus, maxima nihil agentibus

    Most of one thing: maxima pars vītae, most of one’s life.

  • plērumque — mostly, for the most part, usually

    adverb · also used · classical · Plin. Ep. 9.36.1: plērumque circā hōram prīmam; Cic. Off. 1.118: plērumque autem parentium praeceptīs imbūtī

    “Most of the time”.

Examples

  • plēraque sunt vocābula quibus vulgō ūtimur, neque tamen liquidō scīmus quid ea propriē atque vērē significent

    most of the words we use every day, we don’t clearly know what they properly and truly meanGell. 16.5.1

  • quod plēraque nōs illā quasi mūgiente M litterā clūdimus

    because we end most words with that letter M, which sounds almost like mooingQuint. 12.10.30

  • eam plērīque scrīptōrēs, maximē quī sunt ab Isocrate, volunt esse lūcidam, brevem, vērīsimilem

    most writers, especially those of Isocrates’ school, want it to be clear, short and believableQuint. 4.2.31

  • magna pars vītae ēlābitur male agentibus, maxima nihil agentibus, tōta vīta aliud agentibus

    a great part of life slips away while we do wrong, most of it while we do nothing, the whole of it while we do something elseSen. Ep. 1.1

  • ōlim tōnsōrēs nōn fuisse adsignificant antīquōrum statuae, quod plēraeque habent capillum et barbam magnam

    the old statues show that there were once no barbers, since most of them have long hair and a big beardVarr. RR 2.11.10

  • ēvigilō cum libuit, plērumque circā hōram prīmam, saepe ante, tardius rārō

    I wake when I please, mostly about sunrise, often before, seldom laterPlin. Ep. 9.36.1

See also most, a lot, whole, part.

SourcesLewis & Short: plerique · Lewis & Short: magnus (maximus) · Lewis & Short: pars · Lewis & Short: plerumque

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
